frase_gancho.texto: Before cities and gods, there was the question of who we are.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Any history museum could begin with a king or a pyramid. This one begins with a bigger question: what makes us human? In this hall, also called the Hall of Origins, anthropology is presented through its four paths: the body, which is studied by physical anthropology; the traces of the past, which archaeology seeks out; languages; and the customs of the peoples who live today, which is the field of ethnography. With murals, maps, and reconstructions, the hall invites you to see the human species as one family with many ways of living. Everything else, from the mammoth to the last hall upstairs, grows out of this idea.
